questionText: Consider an Ethernet segment with a transmission speed of $10^8$ bits/sec and a maximum segment length of 500 meters. If the speed of propagation of the signal in the medium is $2\times 10^8$ meters/sec, then the minimum frame size (in bits) required for collision detection is ________
explanation:
Given Data:
• Transmission speed ($B$) = $10^8$ bits/sec
• Maximum segment length ($d$) = $500$ meters
• Speed of propagation ($v$) = $2 \times 10^8$ meters/sec

Formula:
For collision detection in CSMA/CD Ethernet, the condition for minimum frame size ($L$) is:
$L = 2 \times T_p \times B$
where $T_p$ is the propagation delay ($T_p = \frac{d}{v}$).

Calculation:
1. Calculate propagation delay ($T_p$):
$T_p = \frac{500 \text{ m}}{2 \times 10^8 \text{ m/sec}} = 2.5 \times 10^{-6} \text{ seconds}$

2. Calculate minimum frame size ($L$):
$L = 2 \times (2.5 \times 10^{-6} \text{ sec}) \times 10^8 \text{ bits/sec}$
$L = 500 \text{ bits}$

Thus, the minimum frame size required for collision detection is 500 bits.
